thread:
DeployBot: Canary gate fail: hosted-api canary (canary-2026-03-23-09) p95 3x baseline and 4xx burst. Auto-rollback attempted but blocked by "canary-gate=manual" policy. https://dash.redwood/alerts/6977 :warning:
Will: saw the canary alarms. The canary is pinned to verify experiment telemetry. Auto-rollback blocked by policy. We need a quick decision: unpin, reroute canary traffic to degraded-model, or manual rollback.
Priya: stack traces show request validation errors from a new schema change in the canary. 4xxs mostly from a client payload shape mismatch. Not a backend perf regression.
OpsLead: important callout: a straight rollback would drop a new response format that some customers already started depending on. Rolling back now could cause client exceptions for those who adapted. Proposal: 1) pause all new canary rollouts; 2) perform a staged traffic cut to a compatibility shim (degraded-model) that returns old shape; 3) if errors persist after 10m, schedule manual rollback in a low-traffic window.
Emil: adding that degraded-model exists and is compatible. It has slightly higher latency but preserves schema. We can route 30% of canary traffic there immediately.
Product: customer impact: a small percent of customers will get validation errors; we should notify the integration owners before changing response shape. CS team is on standby.
Will: I like the degraded-model cut since rollback risks breaking integrators. OpsLead, confirm thresholds to escalate to manual rollback and exact CLI steps to do the staged reroute.
OpsLead: runbook snippet: ```
# emergency compatibility failover
deployctl pause-rollouts --scope=canary-2026-03-23-09
deployctl route-set --canary canary-2026-03-23-09 --mapping=degraded-model:30,canary:70 --until=2026-03-23T11:00Z
# monitor 4xx_rate, p95, client-errors for 10m. If 4xx_rate doesn't drop below 0.5% OR client-errors persist >3m -> schedule manual rollback to rev=2026-03-22-2145 in a low-traffic window (ops approval + release manager)
```
Priya: will watch validation logs and send sample failing payloads to the canary owners.
EngOncall: attaching initial metric snapshot. At 0m: canary p95 3.1x, 4xx_rate 2.3%.
Will: executing staged reroute to degraded-model 30% now. Running: `deployctl route-set --canary canary-2026-03-23-09 --mapping=degraded-model:30,canary:70 --until=2026-03-23T11:00Z`
DeployBot: Action accepted: staged routing update applied. https://deploy.redwood/actions/697777/compat-failover
EngOncall: 2m after reroute: 4xx_rate down to 0.9%, p95 at 1.5x baseline. Client-errors reduced by ~80%. Continuing 10m observation.
Product: pre-drafted integration-owner note: "We observed a transient client validation issue from the recent canary. We routed affected traffic to a compatibility variant to avoid errors; no action needed unless you see anomalies. We'll follow up with postmortem and timeline for re-release." Ready to send pending OpsLead.
OpsLead: keep change window locked for 60m and release-notes freeze. If 4xx < 0.5% and p95 <= 1.4x at end of observation, we'll keep degraded-model in mapping and plan a controlled re-release after fixing schema validation. If not, manual rollback required with OpsLead+ReleaseManager approval.
Will: adding postmortem stub and linking failing payloads: https://docs.redwood/incident/697777-canary-schema-compat. Thanks all for the quick pivot :thumbsup:
